title: Regional governance: communication & enforcement roadmap (draft)
body:
Purpose:

This working doc captures a proposed cross-functional approach for communicating region-pinning changes to internal teams and customers, and the operational enforcement roadmap we will use to move from permissive enforcement to hard enforcement. It focuses on information flows, detection signals, rollback/fallback options, and the minimum audit record required for compliance reviews.

Context / Why this exists:
- Increasing enterprise demand for explicit region residency guarantees (pinning) means we need a repeatable, low-risk path to enable enforcement.
- Legal and sales require evidence that requests stayed in-region and that deviations are auditable.
- Engineering needs clear phases and runbook hooks to avoid outages during enforcement.

Scope:
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated offerings where customer selects a regional residency (region-pin).
- Excludes private on-prem installs (those have separate infra docs).
- Covers: stakeholder comms, enforcement signals, telemetry & evidence collection, rollback policies, operator runbooks, and customer-facing messaging templates.

Stakeholders and Roles (high level):
- Product (owner): define policy, acceptable error rates, and SLO deltas. (owner: Priya Nair)
- Legal/Compliance: approve audit artifacts and escalation rules (owner: Maya T.)
- Solutions / Customer Success: customer comms and enablement (owner: Diego A.)
- Engineering - Private Deployments: implement routing/enforcement, telemetry, and rollouts (owner: Jonah K.)
- SRE / Oncall: operational response and mitigation (primary oncall rotation)

Decision matrix (simple):
- If request region matches customer pin: allow as normal.
- If request region mismatches and customer is in "permissive" group: log and tag, return 200 with header X-Residency-Warning; increment telemetry counter.
- If request region mismatches and customer is in "enforced" group: block request with 403 and error_code RESIDENCY_VIOLATION unless explicit emergency override.
- If request region mismatches and model fallback is available in pinned region: automatically reroute (if latency delta < configured threshold) and record reroute as fallback-evidence.

Enforcement Phases (proposed timeline):
1) Observability-only (2–4 weeks): enable request-region tagging and aggregate daily metrics. No customer-facing changes.
2) Passive warnings (4–8 weeks): For pilot customers, return a non-fatal warning header and surface incidents in Console under "Residency Warnings". Continue accumulating evidence for audits.
3) Controlled enforcement (pilot) (4 weeks per cohort): Small set of contract customers move to enforced mode; automated rollback on signal thresholds; runbook exercised.
4) Gradual expansion (months): Increase enforced population in waves after post-pilot review.
5) Global hard enforcement: default for new customers after announcement and opt-in window.

Telemetry & Audit evidence (minimum):
- request_id (trace id)
- customer_id and customer_pin (region identifier)
- peer_region (detected serving region) and region_source (placement decision: routing, cache, fallback)
- decision_outcome (allowed | warned | blocked | rerouted)
- timestamp (ISO8601) and node_id (hosting zone)
- policy_version and config_hash
- operator_override_id (if present)

Storage & Retention notes:
- Evidence for blocked/warned events must be retained for 1 year in an immutable audit store.
- Aggregates and dashboards can be shorter (90 days).
- Sensitive fields (PII in payloads) must be redacted before storage — we only store headers/metadata.

Alerting and SLO thresholds to trigger rollback:
- If blocked requests lead to >1% failed request rate for an affected customer over a 15-minute window -> auto rollback for that customer to permissive mode and page SRE.
- If global failed request rate attributable to residency enforcement >0.2% for 30 minutes -> pause rollout and open incident.

Runbook excerpts (oncall):
- Initial triage: run query for request_ids with decision_outcome=blocked and customer_id in scope.
- Verify whether model reroute was attempted and whether fallback succeeded.
- If widespread: escalate to Platform Lead and Product. Consider emergency override (feature flag).
- If single-customer: coordinate with Customer Success to evaluate business impact, then rollback per-customer.

Operator tools required:
- Console widget: "Residency incidents" with per-customer filters, sample request traces, and a one-click rollback to permissive mode (audit log written).
- Feature flag system: per-customer pin enforcement toggle with change history.
- Queryable immutable audit store with simple SQL surface for compliance requests.

Customer communication plan (templates below):
- Pre-announcement (30 days before pilot): explain upcoming changes, why region pinning matters, and our staged approach. Include "what you need to test" checklist.
- Pilot notification (14 days before): invite pilot customers, note that they will receive warning headers first and that support will be actively engaged.
- Enforcement notice (7 days before wider enforcement): detail expected behaviors, rollback path, and support channels.
- Incident template: when an enforcement-related outage occurs, notify impacted customers within 1 hour with RCA timeline and remediation steps.

Sample customer checklist (what to test):
- Confirm SDKs propagate region pin headers correctly.
- Send test calls from representative geo IPs.
- Verify behavior for non-idempotent requests when a reroute occurs.
- Validate logs show the X-Residency-Warning header and that request ids align with our trace.

Open questions / risks (need Product + Legal input):
- What constitutes "sufficient evidence" for a legal audit if a fallback reroute happens (do we need payload hashes)?
- Are there geographies with stronger retention or export rules that require longer evidence retention?
- Customer contracts: do we need to update TOS or Dedicated contracts to reflect automatic reroute behavior?
- Billing impacts: how to account for cross-region cost when reroute occurs?

Implementation checkpoints / tickets (suggested):
- Add region_source + decision_outcome to request logs (JIRA-RES-1202).
- Console: residency incidents dashboard (JIRA-RES-1210).
- Feature flag: per-customer enforcement toggle w/ audit (JIRA-RES-1222).
- Immutable audit store schema + retention (JIRA-RES-1250).

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Engineering: prototype warning header and telemetry (owner: Jonah K., target: 2025-10-16).
- Product: finalize decision matrix and acceptance criteria (owner: Priya N., target: 2025-10-09).
- Legal: list audit evidence items and sign-off retention policy (owner: Maya T., target: 2025-10-20).
- CS: pick pilot customers and prepare enablement materials (owner: Diego A., target: 2025-10-23).

Notes/working thoughts (scratch space):
- Consider exposing a machine-readable "residency-evidence" link in the Console that packages a zip with metadata + traces for audits.
- For Hosted customers: evaluate whether we can offer a low-latency in-region cache copy to reduce reroute impact.
- We should test chaos scenarios (simulate regional partitioning) during pilot to validate rollback path.

References and handy queries (operators):
- Quick SQL to find recent warnings: SELECT request_id, customer_id, decision_outcome, timestamp FROM residency_audit WHERE decision_outcome='warned' AND timestamp > now()-INTERVAL '1 day';
- Trace lookup: use trace_id returned in header X-Trace-ID to fetch the full SDK logs (internal doc link CONFLUENCE-9876).

Appendix: sample headers returned on permissive vs enforced:
- Permissive warning example: X-Residency-Warning: served-from=eu-west-1;policy=2025-10;decision=warned
- Enforced block example: status=403;body={"error":"RESIDENCY_VIOLATION","expected_region":"eu-west-1"}

This doc should be used as the canonical communication + enforcement roadmap draft. Feedback welcome — add comments inline or ping in #sovereign-residency.

Last edited by Aisha Patel on 2026-03-10.
